result:
I'd make humans *actually* want to understand how things work, at a deep level, instead of just wanting to be right or feel good.

Most of the world's self-inflicted damage comes from motivated reasoning, tribal loyalty, and the preference for comforting stories over accurate maps. If that single orientation shifted — if curiosity and reality-testing became the default psychological posture instead of an occasional hobby — a lot of the other problems (bad governance, pseudoscience, pointless wars, short-term destruction of the environment) would become much harder to sustain. People would still disagree, still be flawed, still have competing interests. But the baseline for what counts as a serious argument would be higher.

Everything else is downstream of how seriously we treat the question "Is this actually true?"
